extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary schools), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and institutional legal/ compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on designing and implementing grievance procedures to address sex discrimination and sex-based harassment under Title IX across elementary, secondary, and postsecondary settings, balancing promptness, due process, trauma-informed practices, and alignment with other civil-rights/ employment frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptness of grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 106.45 and 106.46 specifically require a recipient to address complaints of sex discrimination and sex-based harassment “prompt[ly].” (§§106.45(a)(1), 106.46(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department disagrees that these procedures would unnecessarily delay resolution or prevent a recipient from removing a respondent who presents a threat; the regulations have been modified to address concerns about length of time to impose discipline. Recipients must act promptly while complying with procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to remove or place on leave during pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations permit a recipient to remove a respondent from its education program or activity on an emergency basis in certain circumstances (§106.44(h)), or place an employee respondent on administrative leave during the pendency of grievance procedures (§106.44(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance procedures do not preclude prompt action to respond to threats; see discussion of §106.44(g)(2) and (3), (h), (i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures tailored to sex discrimination's distinct considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures adopted in the 2020 amendments and revised here are specifically suited and necessary to address allegations of sex discrimination, which involve considerations distinct from many other student conduct offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These include safeguards to ensure an educational environment free from sex discrimination during the pendency of procedures; recipients must apply these tailored procedures even where other student conduct rules exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of supportive measures and informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinator duties include offering and coordinating supportive measures and, if available and appropriate, offering to resolve a complaint using an informal resolution process (§106.44(f)(1)(ii), (iv), (g), (k)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of confidential resources and informal resolution mitigates any deterrent effect grievance procedures might have; recipients retain discretion to offer informal resolution for most allegations (§§106.44(k), 106.45(k), 106.46(j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of overly quasi-judicial or adversarial processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations remove requirements that appear quasi-judicial or mimic criminal/civil legal systems; they establish a baseline usable by non-attorneys and deemphasize quasi-judicial elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not courts, recipients must administer grievance procedures designed to reach reliable factual determinations promptly and equitably. The final regulations allow discretion to be more or less adversarial (e.g., whether to hold live hearings (§106.46(g)) and how questioning occurs (§§106.45(g), 106.46(f))).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility to evaluate and remedy sex discrimination (even when criminal aspects exist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX requires a recipient to evaluate, and as necessary address, allegations that sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment, has deprived a complainant of equal access to education, and remedy such situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX does not replace redress through civil litigation or criminal process; recipients are often uniquely positioned to implement educational remedies (scheduling, living arrangements, extracurricular access, disciplinary sanctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and alignment with other civil rights laws OCR enforces
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations are limited to Title IX and impose no new requirements for Title VI, Section 504, or the ADA, but set grievance procedure requirements to align more closely with standards used to address harassment under other statutes OCR enforces (e.g., hostile environment analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must comply with all applicable regulations for allegations involving multiple bases; see 34 CFR 104.7(b) and related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of complaints alleging discrimination on multiple bases
rubrics_metrics.description: A single complaint can raise allegations of discrimination on multiple bases. If all allegations relate to sex discrimination (e.g., sexual orientation and gender identity), they can be made in a single complaint and resolved under Title IX grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When allegations involve sex and other bases, recipients must handle sex discrimination allegations under Title IX procedures but are not required to handle non-sex-discrimination allegations under Title IX; recipients have discretion to use a single procedure provided it complies with applicable laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age-appropriate and developmentally appropriate procedures for K-12
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures for elementary and secondary schools must account for the particular context and younger student population; less complex procedures, such as oral complaints without signatures, are appropriate and developmentally suitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents/guardians have the legal right to be present and assist their child in K-12 Title IX procedures (§106.6(g)); the Department does not require live hearings at the K-12 level and recognizes recipients may need flexibility in communicating definitions and procedures to younger students and parents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting minor complainants from repeated or traumatizing questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the regulations requires a recipient to repeatedly question a complainant who may be a minor about alleged sex discrimination, which could be traumatizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may consult/partner with organizations experienced in trauma-informed child sexual abuse investigations (e.g., child advocacy centers, multidisciplinary teams) consistent with §106.44(j). Questions asked must be relevant and not otherwise impermissible under §§106.2 and 106.45(b)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to communicate using age-appropriate terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient retains discretion in how it communicates with students, parents, and other stakeholders about what constitutes sex discrimination and how grievance procedures operate, so long as it effectively conveys obligations and rights under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the exact regulatory terminology facilitates enforcement comparisons, but recipients may use different terminology as appropriate for age, maturity, and educational level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process baseline requirements for K-12 consistent with Supreme Court precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures include notice and an opportunity for the respondent to be heard before imposition of discipline, aligning with Goss v. Lopez's minimal due process requirements (e.g., notice of allegations; opportunity to present fact witnesses and relevant evidence; access to and the opportunity to respond to relevant evidence; compliance with grievance procedures before imposing disciplinary sanctions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific regulatory citations: §106.45(c) (notice of allegations), (f)(2) (equal opportunity to present fact witnesses and relevant evidence), (f)(4) (access and response to evidence), (h)(4) (compliance before discipline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may use existing processes that satisfy §106.45
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations prohibits a recipient from using an existing process that otherwise satisfies the requirements of §106.45 to investigate and resolve Title IX complaints (e.g., State anti-bullying or student-discipline laws).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an existing process complies with §106.45 requirements, it may be used; however, the Department maintains a uniform Federal standard for Title IX compliance and a recipient must fulfill Title IX obligations even if state laws differ (§106.6(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX applicability to employees and interaction with Title VII/collective bargaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX applies to employees as well as students; recipients must implement grievance procedures consistent with §106.45 for employee-involved complaints, and postsecondary institutions have an additional obligation to implement §106.46 where either complainant or respondent is a student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may align Title IX procedures with Title VII processes, collective bargaining agreements, or employee handbooks as long as they do not conflict with §§106.45/106.46. If conflicts arise, Title IX obligations must be fulfilled (§106.6(b)). Differences between Title VII and Title IX can justify different procedural protections and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline standards for fairness, impartiality, and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for grievance procedures under §106.45 set baseline standards to ensure a fair process under Title IX, including equitable treatment of parties; decisionmakers free of bias or conflicts of interest; adequate notice of allegations and timeframes; guidelines for adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation; opportunity for parties to present evidence; and guidelines for how decisionmakers assess evidence and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These baseline protections aim to promote reliable factual determinations and equitable treatment across recipients; many recipients may already have similar protections, but the final regulations standardize these baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion over procedural features influencing adversarialness
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 106.45 and 106.46 provide recipients discretion to create grievance procedures that may be more or less adversarial, such as deciding whether to hold live hearings (§106.46(g)) or how parties and witnesses are questioned (§§106.45(g), 106.46(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may tailor the level of adversarial procedure to context (age of students, nature of allegations) while still meeting Title IX requirements for reliability and equity.
